steps.player: Thanks. Hmmm, do you know something? This rope has a funny smell.

steps.npc: Really?

steps.player: Yes, It reminds me of...yaks. I was travelling in the Fremennik Isles recently and, do you know what? They made rope out of yak's hair.

steps.npc: What a coincidence?

steps.player: There was a lady over there who sold wool, she said she traded rope for the wool.

steps.npc: Who would have thought it?

steps.player: I don't think you make rope at all. I think you trade balls of wool for rope.

steps.npc: Oh, I confess. You have found the truth. I used to make the rope myself, but my fingers aren't as nimble as they used to be and so many people wanted my rope. Demand was so high I had to find another
source. But I couldn't tell anyone since Ned's Handmade Rope (100% Wool) is a high profile brand now.

steps.player: Yes, well, the wool is still pretty good, though yak hair makes fine rope. I don't suppose any harm will come of it.

value.player: I'm looking for a quest.

value.text: On quest speedrunning worlds:

steps.speaker: Fred the Farmer
steps.text: You're after a quest, you say? Well I don't have any here.
This quest is not available on Speedrunning Worlds.

value.speaker: Fred the Farmer
value.text: You're after a quest, you say? Actually, I could do with a bit of help.

value.speaker: Fred the Farmer
value.text: My sheep are getting mighty woolly. I'd be much obliged if you could shear them. And while you're at it, spin the wool for me too.

value.speaker: Fred the Farmer
value.text: Yes, that's it. Bring me 20 balls of wool. And I'm sure I could sort out some sort of payment. Of course, there's the small matter of The Thing.

value.player: What do you mean, The Thing?

value.speaker: Fred the Farmer
value.text: Well now, no one has ever seen The Thing. That's why we call it The Thing, 'cos we don't know what it is.

value.speaker: Fred the Farmer
value.text: Some say it's a black hearted shapeshifter, hungering for the souls of hard working decent folk like me. Others say it's just a sheep.

value.speaker: Fred the Farmer
value.text: Well I don't have all day to stand around and gossip. Are you going to shear my sheep or what!

steps.player: Yes, okay. I can do that.

steps.text: If the player already has 20 balls of wool in their inventory:

steps.player: In fact Fred, funnily enough, I actually have 20 balls of wool already on me.

steps.speaker: Fred the Farmer
steps.text: Have you been shearing my sheep without permission!?

steps.player: No! Well, maybe... They just looked a little wooly! Surely you like a shave once in a while, too?

steps.speaker: Fred the Farmer
steps.text: It's rude to shave another person without permission - don't be coming at me with them shears!

steps.player: I'm sorry, I'll ask permission next time.

steps.speaker: Fred the Farmer
steps.text: I guess no real 'arm was done. Hand the balls over and we can put this whole thing behind us.
You give Fred 20 balls of wool.

steps.player: That's the last of them.

steps.speaker: Fred the Farmer
steps.text: I guess I'd better pay you then.
Quest complete!

steps.speaker: Fred the Farmer
steps.text: Good! Now one more thing, do you actually know how to shear a sheep?

steps.player: Err. No, I don't know actually.

steps.text: If the player doesn't have shears:

steps.speaker: Fred the Farmer
steps.text: Well, first things first, you need a pair of shears. I've got some here you can use.

steps.speaker: Fred the Farmer
steps.text: You just need to go and use them on the sheep out in my field.

steps.player: Sounds easy!

steps.speaker: Fred the Farmer
steps.text: That's what they all say!

steps.speaker: Fred the Farmer
steps.text: Some of the sheep don't like it too much... Persistence is the key.

steps.speaker: Fred the Farmer
steps.text: Once you've collected some wool you can spin it into balls.

steps.speaker: Fred the Farmer
steps.text: Well, you're half way there already! You have a set of shears in your inventory. Just use those on a Sheep to shear it.

steps.player: That's all I have to do?

steps.speaker: Fred the Farmer
steps.text: Well once you've collected some wool you'll need to spin it into balls.

steps.speaker: Fred the Farmer
steps.text: Do you know how to spin wool?

steps.player: I don't know how to spin wool, sorry.

steps.speaker: Fred the Farmer
steps.text: Don't worry, it's quite simple!

steps.speaker: Fred the Farmer

steps.speaker: Fred the Farmer
steps.text: To get to Lumbridge Castle just follow the road east.

steps.player: Thank you!

steps.text: Suit yourself.

value.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
value.text: Welcome to the museum of Varrock.

value.player: Hello there. I'm here about the Shield of Arrav.

value.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
value.text: The Shield of Arrav? The Museum has been searching for that for years! The late King Roald II offered a generous reward for its return!

value.player: Well, I'm here to claim it.

value.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
value.text: You've found the shield? Let's have a look!
You show the shield half to the curator.

value.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
value.text: This is incredible! But where's the other half?

value.player: I obtained this half from the [Phoenix Gang/Black Arm Gang]. The [Black Arm Gang/Phoenix Gang] might have the other half.

value.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
value.text: That does sound plausible. We will have to hope that another adventurer can recover that half.

value.player: So will I be rewarded for recovering half of the shield?

value.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
value.text: I'm afraid the reward is for the recovery of the full shield. However, what I'll do is write you out two half- certificates. If another adventurer returns the other shield half, I'll do the same for them.

value.speaker: Curator Haig Halen
value.text: The two of you can then swap one of the half- certificates to make a full one each. Take that to the King and he will grant you your reward.
The curator gives you two half-certificates.

options.text: Tell me more about the Archive.

steps.player: Tell me more about the Archive.

steps.npc: You can see the Archive's layout on the board beside me. The central chamber, which we're calling the Nexus, is currently occupied by a hostile automaton. We plan to take that chamber and establish our defences there.

steps.player: And by 'we' you mean me?

steps.npc: Indeed. Before he left, Armacus informed me you would clear the way whilst he and the others mobilised the rest of the troops.

steps.player: He did, did he?

steps.npc: Yes! He seemed confident you would help. 'I can see it in [his/her] eyes. The flame of justice!'
He is a bit eccentric, but he is a fine leader, and a good judge of character.

steps.player: At least one of those is true. What comes after the Nexus?

steps.npc: There are six peripheral chambers we expect to come under attack, all of which can be reached from the Nexus. As soon as the Nexus is secured, we will begin deploying troops to the furthest chambers.
They will hold the line whilst we work on clearing the foremost ones. We are relying on you to take one side whilst we take the other.

steps.player: So that makes... the Nexus plus three chambers you want taking care of?

steps.npc: Yes. It is no small ask, but we do not think we can manage any more ourselves. I would suggest you seek allies of your own to help you.

steps.player: I'll see what I can do.
Who are our enemies?

steps.npc: We have followers of Lucien, Zamorak and Bandos to deal with. Evidence also suggests there are other foes yet to fully reveal themselves. For example, there have been reports of a lone knight.

steps.player: A lone knight?

steps.npc: Yes. The scouting report is spotty. Only one of our people made it back alive, but they were heavily wounded. Apparently this knight took out a whole squadron by himself.

steps.player: That's concerning... What about the others?

steps.npc: The Bandosian forces are mostly goblins. You wouldn't think they'd pose much of a threat, but they've managed to build some sort of siege engine. If that weren't enough, they're being lead by a huge ork.
As for the forces of Lucien and Zamorak, we spotted a clash between the two factions in some of the deeper tunnels. An army of skeletons facing off against a group of Zamorakian mages.

steps.player: The Dagon'hai?

steps.npc: Interestingly, no, but we'll get to them. We managed to capture one of the mages and interrogate them. They refused to say much, but we gather they're trying to summon some sort of powerful demon.

steps.player: And the skeletons?

steps.npc: There seems to be an endless tide of them. A necromancer must be present. It's possible this is the work of Moia, the leader of Lucien's forces.

steps.player: And let me guess, there's more?

steps.npc: Quite... You mentioned the Dagon'hai. A group of them were spotted near the Stone of Jas' old location. They seemed to be fending off an unusually capable tormented demon.

steps.player: In what way?

steps.npc: Most tormented demons seem to struggle with the strength of their own flames. This one seemed to fully control them, lending it both greater power and durability.

steps.player: Did it manage to get rid of the Dagon'hai?

steps.npc: No, they disengaged and made for a tunnel we think leads to the Archive. The demon followed, but went down a different path.

steps.player: That's quite the list we're up against.

steps.npc: Yes... but we are not without allies either. The Alliance is rallying as we speak. Together we can do this.

steps.player: Where is everybody else?

steps.npc: Armacus, Eva and Ivy have gone to rally the rest of the forces. We are only a small vanguard sent to assess the situation and prepare if necessary.

steps.player: Let's hope they don't take too long.

steps.npc: Fear not, they will soon return with help. Once they are here, we estimate we can defeat three sets of intruders. As for the rest... we will be relying on you and any allies you can gather yourself.

standard-dialogue.npc: I'm not sure... What is it you're interrupting me for?

standard-dialogue.player: Well, I was just going to ask what you're doing, but I'm starting to regret it.

standard-dialogue.npc: Why didn't you say so, my dear!
I... am... the Keeper of the Records!
These sensitive records are under my precise curation!
The secrets of the Archive, the progress of the Alliance, the very steps you took towards me today, all recorded in these... very... pages!
Hmm... I suppose you may view some of the records, should your curiosity need satisfying.
